chunks: And the married women among the women are forbidden to you, except those whom your right hands possess, as a decree of God upon you. And lawful for you are those beyond these, if you seek them with your wealth for wedlock and not for debauchery. Then give those of these women you have enjoyed, the agreed dower as a duty. And there is no sin upon you in what you mutually agree to after the duty, for God is certainly All-Knowing, All-Wise.

key_terms.أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ: If you seek them with your wealth (dower)
key_terms.إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ: Except those whom your right hands possess (captives/concubines)
key_terms.فِيمَا تَرَاضَيْتُمْ بِهِ: In what you mutually agreed upon

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between marriage and concubinage regarding dower and permission in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is central to understanding the permissibility of temporary marriage (Mut'ah), as the term 'istimta'' (enjoyment) and the requirement of 'ujrah' (dower) are interpreted as specific indicators of this institution. It distinguishes between permanent marriage and concubinage by emphasizing that lawful sexual relations, whether through wedlock or concubage, require financial compensation and exclusivity from fornication. The verse underscores divine wisdom in regulating marital relations, ensuring that unions are formalized contracts rather than casual liaisons.
